answer: A place I visit almost every day is a small gym near my home, which has become an important part of my routine. It is on the ground floor of a building just two streets away from our flat, so I can walk there in five minutes. I started going a couple of years ago to improve my health, after I realised that sitting at a desk all day was giving me back pain, and it quickly became a habit I genuinely look forward to. It is nothing fancy, but it is clean, well-equipped and rarely too crowded. I usually go straight after work and spend about an hour there, doing a mix of weights and running on the treadmill, followed by some stretching. It is one of the few times my mind switches off completely. What keeps me coming back is how [[energising]] a workout is after a long day at a desk. There is also a real sense of [[camaraderie]] among the regulars, which makes it feel welcoming rather than intimidating; we encourage each other and sometimes argue about cricket between sets. The trainer knows everyone by name, and he has been very patient with me. Beyond the physical benefits, it has become a valuable [[outlet for stress]]. Honestly, going there consistently has been genuinely [[transformative]] for both my body and my mood, and even my mother says I seem more cheerful these days. I think having a place that keeps you [[disciplined]] and healthy is worth its weight in gold.

followUps.q: Do you prefer exercising alone or with others?
followUps.answer: I actually like a mix. I do my workout on my own, but having other people around keeps me motivated, and it is always easier to push yourself when someone is cheering you on.

followUps.q: Are gyms popular where you live?
followUps.answer: They have become much more popular in recent years. When I was younger, hardly anyone in Sirajganj went to a gym, but now several have opened, and they are mostly full of young people.
